regime_interpretation: Scarcity-led upper-tail regime where low renewable output required very high gas generation, raising the probability of imbalance price spikes.
paper_use: Use as the main 2025 upper-tail case study. This event demonstrates how extreme price spikes can emerge from the combination of very high gas generation, very low wind and sharp intraday price jumps.

regime_interpretation: Scarcity-led upper-tail regime where low renewable output required very high gas generation, raising the probability of imbalance price spikes.
paper_use: Use as a secondary January scarcity case. It supports the argument that January 2025 contained repeated scarcity episodes rather than a single isolated event.

regime_interpretation: Scarcity-led upper-tail regime where low renewable output required very high gas generation, raising the probability of imbalance price spikes.
paper_use: Use to show morning-ramp scarcity. This case is useful because the spike formed outside the main evening peak.

regime_interpretation: System-stress regime where positive imbalance amplified price formation, especially when combined with low wind or reduced interconnector support.
paper_use: Use to show that 2025 spike risk was not purely a winter phenomenon. The event links positive imbalance and low interconnector support to summer mixed-tail stress.

regime_interpretation: Near-scarcity regime where physical tightness was present but did not always convert into an extreme spike.
paper_use: Use as a near-spike comparison case. This helps explain why stressed conditions sometimes stop below the main £250/MWh spike threshold.

paper_use: Use as the main autumn transition case. It shows renewed upper-tail stress under very low wind, high gas and positive imbalance.

regime_interpretation: Mixed-transition regime where several drivers interacted but no single dominant scarcity mechanism fully explains the case.
paper_use: Use as a short evening-spike example during the October transition regime.

regime_interpretation: Near-scarcity regime where physical tightness was present but did not always convert into an extreme spike.
paper_use: Use as another October evening case to show repeated autumn mixed-transition stress.

regime_interpretation: Lower-tail surplus regime where negative imbalance, high wind and/or weak thermal demand created downward pressure on imbalance prices.
paper_use: Use as a major negative-price case showing strong downward-price formation under very negative imbalance and high wind.
